title: Impact of Medicare Eligibility on Hospital Visits

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) at the age-65 Medicare eligibility cutoff.
- Why: Eligibility switches sharply at 65, creating quasi-random treatment near the threshold. Comparing individuals just below vs. just above 65 identifies the local average treatment effect of Medicare eligibility on log hospital visits.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of log hospital visits is smooth in age at the cutoff (no other discontinuities exactly at 65).
  - No precise manipulation: Individuals cannot precisely sort age around 65 to select into treatment.
  - Locality: Effect is identified locally; bandwidth needs to be small enough to ensure comparability but large enough for precision.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load and analyze: Sharp RDD of Medicare eligibility at 65 on log hospital visits
# File path: experiments/exp_b/data/s86_data.csv

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s86_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Basic sanity checks
stopifnot(all(c("running_var","treated","y","near_cutoff") %in% names(df)))
cat("Rows read:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Share treated:", round(mean(df$treated), 3), "\n")
cat("Mean y (log visits):", round(mean(df$y), 3), "\n")

# 2) Construct a signed running variable (distance from cutoff)
# The file provides 'running_var' as a (scaled) distance from 65.
# We infer side using treatment status (sharp assignment near 65).
x_abs <- df$running_var
D <- df$treated
y <- df$y
# Signed distance: negative below cutoff (D=0), positive above (D=1)
s <- ifelse(D == 1, x_abs, -x_abs)

# Scale
maxs <- max(abs(s), na.rm = TRUE)

# 3) Local linear RD helper
rd_local_linear <- function(y, D, s, h, order = 1, donut = 0, kernel = "triangular") {
  idx <- which(is.finite(y) & is.finite(D) & is.finite(s) &
                 abs(s) <= h & abs(s) > donut)
  if (length(idx) < 30) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, ci = c(NA, NA), n = length(idx), h = h,
                order = order, donut = donut))
  }
  ys <- y[idx]; Ds <- D[idx]; ss <- s[idx]
  # Weights
  if (kernel == "triangular") {
    w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(ss)/h)
  } else {
    w <- rep(1, length(ss))
  }
  dat <- data.frame(y = ys, D = Ds, s = ss)
  if (order == 1) {
    fit <- lm(y ~ D + s + D:s, data = dat, weights = w)
  } else {
    dat$s2 <- dat$s^2
    fit <- lm(y ~ D + s + s2 + D:s + D:s2, data = dat, weights = w)
  }
  coefs <- summary(fit)$coef
  # Guard in case of collinearity
  if (!"D" %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, ci = c(NA, NA), n = nrow(dat), h = h,
                order = order, donut = donut))
  }
  tau <- coefs["D", "Estimate"]
  se <- coefs["D", "Std. Error"]
  tcrit <- qt(0.975, df = fit$df.residual)
  ci <- c(tau - tcrit * se, tau + tcrit * se)
  list(tau = as.numeric(tau), se = as.numeric(se), ci = as.numeric(ci),
       n = nrow(dat), h = h, order = order, donut = donut)
}

fmt <- function(x, d = 4) ifelse(is.na(x), NA, formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))

# 4) Main specification: local linear with triangular kernel and moderate bandwidth
h_main <- 0.30 * maxs
res_main <- rd_local_linear(y, D, s, h = h_main, order = 1)

# 5) Robustness checks
# (a) Alternative bandwidths
h_small <- 0.20 * maxs
h_large <- 0.40 * maxs
res_h_small <- rd_local_linear(y, D, s, h = h_small, order = 1)
res_h_large <- rd_local_linear(y, D, s, h = h_large, order = 1)

# (b) Quadratic in running variable
res_quad <- rd_local_linear(y, D, s, h = h_main, order = 2)

# (c) Donut hole exclusion very near the cutoff
donut <- 0.02 * maxs
res_donut <- rd_local_linear(y, D, s, h = h_main, order = 1, donut = donut)

# (d) Placebo cutoff away from 65 (should show no jump)
s0 <- 0.20 * maxs
Dp <- as.integer(s >= s0)     # pseudo "treated" relative to placebo cutoff
sp <- s - s0                  # signed distance from placebo cutoff
res_placebo <- rd_local_linear(y, Dp, sp, h = 0.20 * maxs, order = 1)

# (e) Predetermined near-cutoff sample window provided by data
if ("near_cutoff" %in% names(df)) {
  idx_near <- which(df$near_cutoff == 1 & is.finite(y) & is.finite(D) & is.finite(s))
  if (length(idx_near) >= 30) {
    fit_near <- lm(y ~ D + s + D:s, data = data.frame(y = y[idx_near],
                                                       D = D[idx_near],
                                                       s = s[idx_near]))
    coefs_near <- summary(fit_near)$coef
    tau_near <- if ("D" %in% rownames(coefs_near)) coefs_near["D","Estimate"] else NA
    se_near  <- if ("D" %in% rownames(coefs_near)) coefs_near["D","Std. Error"] else NA
    tcrit_near <- if (!is.na(se_near)) qt(0.975, df = fit_near$df.residual) else NA
    ci_near <- if (!is.na(se_near)) c(tau_near - tcrit_near*se_near, tau_near + tcrit_near*se_near) else c(NA, NA)
  } else {
    tau_near <- se_near <- ci_near <- NA
  }
} else {
  tau_near <- se_near <- ci_near <- NA
}

# 6) Print results
cat("\n==== Main RD Estimate (Local Linear, Triangular) ====\n")
cat("Bandwidth h =", fmt(res_main$h, 3), " | N =", res_main$n, "\n")
cat("Tau (effect on log visits):", fmt(res_main$tau, 4),
    "  SE:", fmt(res_main$se, 4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(res_main$ci[1], 4), ",", fmt(res_main$ci[2], 4), "]\n")

cat("\n-- Bandwidth Robustness --\n")
cat("Small h =", fmt(res_h_small$h,3), " | N =", res_h_small$n,
    " | Tau:", fmt(res_h_small$tau,4), " SE:", fmt(res_h_small$se,4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(res_h_small$ci[1],4), ",", fmt(res_h_small$ci[2],4), "]\n")
cat("Large h =", fmt(res_h_large$h,3), " | N =", res_h_large$n,
    " | Tau:", fmt(res_h_large$tau,4), " SE:", fmt(res_h_large$se,4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(res_h_large$ci[1],4), ",", fmt(res_h_large$ci[2],4), "]\n")

cat("\n-- Polynomial Robustness (Quadratic) --\n")
cat("h =", fmt(res_quad$h,3), " | N =", res_quad$n,
    " | Tau:", fmt(res_quad$tau,4), " SE:", fmt(res_quad$se,4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(res_quad$ci[1],4), ",", fmt(res_quad$ci[2],4), "]\n")

cat("\n-- Donut Hole Robustness --\n")
cat("h =", fmt(res_donut$h,3), " donut =", fmt(res_donut$donut,3), " | N =", res_donut$n,
    " | Tau:", fmt(res_donut$tau,4), " SE:", fmt(res_donut$se,4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(res_donut$ci[1],4), ",", fmt(res_donut$ci[2],4), "]\n")

cat("\n-- Placebo Cutoff Check --\n")
cat("Placebo h =", fmt(res_placebo$h,3), " | N =", res_placebo$n,
    " | Tau:", fmt(res_placebo$tau,4), " SE:", fmt(res_placebo$se,4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(res_placebo$ci[1],4), ",", fmt(res_placebo$ci[2],4), "]\n")

cat("\n-- Provided Near-Cutoff Window (Unweighted OLS) --\n")
cat("N (near_cutoff==1):", ifelse(is.null(length(idx_near)), NA, length(idx_near)), "\n")
cat("Tau:", fmt(tau_near,4), " SE:", fmt(se_near,4),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(ci_near[1],4), ",", fmt(ci_near[2],4), "]\n")

# 7) Also report implied percent change for main estimate
if (!is.na(res_main$tau)) {
  pct <- 100 * (exp(res_main$tau) - 1)
  cat("\nImplied percent change in hospital visits at 65 (main spec):", fmt(pct, 2), "%\n")
}

# End
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive (an increase in log hospital visits at age 65). Medicare reduces the price of care and expands coverage, typically increasing utilization at the eligibility threshold.
- Magnitude: A modest rise, roughly 5–15% in hospital visits (i.e., 0.05–0.14 log points), localized around the cutoff.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare individuals just below and above age 65.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Medicare eligibility at age 65 leads to a reduction in hospital visits.
